# Agent guide: baton

baton is a CLI-first continuity layer for coding agents (TypeScript, Node ≥ 22.13). Read `.context/STATE.md` first, then `docs/roadmap.md` for the current phase.

## Commands

- `npm run check` — lint (Biome), typecheck, tests (Vitest). Must pass before a task is done.
- `npm run build` — bundle to `dist/baton.mjs` and sync `plugin/dist/`.
- `npm run validate:skills` — Agent Skills spec check for `plugin/skills/`.
- `node dist/baton.mjs --help` — the CLI contract. `node dist/baton.mjs task ready` — what to work on next.

## Project rules

- `src/core/` is pure logic and small IO wrappers; it never imports from `commands/`, `hooks/` or `mcp/`.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 check failed/blocked, 3 not implemented.
- Hooks fail open (stderr + exit 0); only structured denies change agent behaviour.
- New harness facts go in `docs/research/2026-10-16-implementation-notes.md` with a source and a status.
- Skills use Agent Skills spec keys only.

## Continuity rules

- Do not edit `.context/STATE.md` or files in `.context/decisions/` directly. STATE is generated; ADRs are append-only (supersede with a new record).
- Load-bearing choices (dependencies, formats, hook semantics) get an ADR before code.
- No markdown TODO lists. Work items live in the task store: `baton task ready`, `baton task update <id> --claim`, `baton task create "..."`, `baton task close <id>`. Never edit `.context/tasks.jsonl` or `.context/memories.jsonl` by hand.

## Where things are

- Intent: `.context/spec.md` · Why: `.context/decisions/` · Gotchas: `.context/knowledge/`
- Design: `docs/design/` (architecture, context format, metrics) · Evidence: `docs/research/`
